title: Black Jack
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Osamu Tezuka's classic follows Black Jack, a genius surgeon without a license who charges enormous fees and is seen as a heartless rogue, in hundreds of self-contained stories. He often treats the poor for free or humbles the arrogant, and some tales end with good people facing death to save others. He lives with Pinoko, a girl he built from a removed teratoma, and clashes with Dr. Kiriko, a doctor who practices euthanasia.
life_message: Life is precious and worth fighting for, and true healing comes from skill joined to conscience rather than status or rules.

Order vs freedom.evidence: An unlicensed surgeon who clashes with the medical establishment (publisher blurb).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Medical science is central, though ghosts appear in some stories.

folkways.japan: Tezuka trained in medicine, and the series critiques Japan's rigid medical hierarchy of its era while keeping its taciturn hero's quiet devotion.

delivery.evidence: Wikipedia: most stories show a good deed or teach the arrogant humility; often used in Japanese schools for educational value (to verify).

personified.ideology: fight for every life, outside the rules

delivery.note: Dr. Kiriko is a rival whose euthanasia stance is given real motives (wartime suffering) and who sometimes cooperates with Black Jack, so the opposing view is personified but not cartoonish.

winners_losers: Black Jack's fight for life usually wins sympathy; Kiriko's euthanasia is opposed but given reasons, and arrogant elites are humbled.
